title: avd-remediation-plan/v1: the ordered changes one assessment and its review call for (plan.json)
description: Contract C24, written by avd-current-state's assessment portal from a C21 report, its C23 review if there is one, and the method's remediation hints (C20). One item per finding to fix: the Fix rows of the review, or every non-pass check when there is no review. Each item cites what good is and why (avd-assess claims) and names the change: an avd-landing-zone parameter or setting, or manual with a code. It holds no names, IDs or free text, only the estate pseudonym, check IDs and public values, and works without the brain or avd-swarm, which may import it (optional extensions only). The method is avd-assess methods/remediation.md.

publicValue.description: A public value only: a SKU, a count, a boolean, a region. Never a name, prefix or address: a string starts with a letter and holds only letters, digits and underscores, so an address, a CIDR prefix or a hyphenated resource name can't pass.

estate.description: The same pseudonym as the C21 report

basis.description: What the plan came from: the SHA-256 of the C21 report's bytes, the C23 review's when there was one, and the method version the report ran

landingZoneCommit.description: The avd-landing-zone commit the lz-parameter and lz-setting changes refer to

items.description: At most one item per check. 'order' runs 1, 2, 3 ... by the rule in avd-assess methods/remediation.md: gap, then warn, then unknown; then severity high, medium, low; then check ID. tests/check_contracts.py checks the example against it.

outcome.description: The C21 outcome; a passing check never makes an item

claims.description: The check's avd-assess citations: what good is and why

source.description: review-fix: the reviewer chose Fix; unreviewed: the check has no review row (or there is no review), so a non-pass check is planned as a fix (as C23 says)

from.description: The value the estate has now, when it is public and known

extensions.description: Optional, for upper layers only, keyed by namespace (contracts/README.md rule 1). A foundation reader ignores it.
